approved_spoken_answer: For most tax-assistance applications you'll want a few basics: a photo ID, proof that you live in the home — like a utility bill — proof of income for everyone in the household, and your most recent tax notice if you have one. Don't worry if you're missing something; we can note what you have and what still needs gathering.
long_answer: Common documents for Wayne County and Detroit tax-relief applications (HOPE, PAYS, payment plans) include: government-issued photo ID; proof of residency such as a utility bill or lease; proof of household income (pay stubs, benefit statements, or tax returns) for all adults in the home; the property tax notice or parcel number; and, where relevant, proof of ownership such as a deed. Specific programs may request additional items; application assistance partners can help assemble them.
disclaimer: Exact document requirements are set by each program and may vary.

approved_spoken_answer: You can pay Wayne County property taxes online, by mail, or in person at the Treasurer's Office at 400 Monroe Street in downtown Detroit. Online is usually fastest, and you can also check your balance there any time with your parcel number or address.
long_answer: Wayne County delinquent property taxes can be paid: online through the Treasurer's payment portal (card or e-check, fees may apply); by mail to the Wayne County Treasurer, 400 Monroe, Detroit, MI 48226; or in person at the Treasurer's Office. Current-year taxes are paid to your local city or township until they become delinquent. Balances and payment history are available through the Treasurer's online property lookup.
disclaimer: Payment channels and fees are set by the Wayne County Treasurer and your local treasurer.
